top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Hanson, Dorn) rests on a first-order question, who bears the adjustment costs when trade and technology change labour demand, answered with transparent designs that have been replicated, re-analysed and contested for about a decade. The contested parts concern the size and persistence of effects, not whether adjustment is slow and costly. Autor, Dorn and Hanson are joint authors of the central China-shock papers, so the three-name credit is accurate if the citation is confined to the empirical evidence and does not claim the task-model theory whose originators lie outside the credited set. P002 (Melitz, Helpman) is a mature, cleanly credited and well-confirmed alternative that I would support, though its welfare conclusions depend on functional form and Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum lie outside the pair. The two cover different ground, and I give more weight to consequences for people and places. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Hanson, Dorn, Helpman or Melitz. Disclosed but not adjudicated: my 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity is thematically adjacent to P001, and V-Dem and QoG colleagues are not credited names.
